source_text:
Can you please look at https://zone.hyperreal.enterprises/wip/notebooks/daxiang_live.html and help extend it?  It starts by saying "The agent's turn is read by 大象" and I'd like it so that not *just* the agent's turn but the turn and surrounding context (I think that's already the case, but if so the notebook isn't clear).  NB. also that patterns are linked by both @why and @how edges, so they can provide both rationale and pratical-implementation links (in particular, @how is more similar to Alexander's notion of child patterns).  Overall I'd like to make various practical improvements to both the system and this notebook, possibly by making the "next steps" in the notebook concrete.   I'd also like to bring the material from the "staging" site on to the master branch defined by futon7a so we can make the notebook public.  We don't have to do that immediately; what do you think we should change before it goes public?  Note that that itself is a contextual question, i.e., this has to be discoverable from index.html.  I think the index.html pointers in the section 

"We can remember it for you, bespoke."

are OK... but it should be suitably caveated.  I.e. 

We've been building highly customised memory systems for working on software and mathematics tasks that need complex graphical inference. Standard coding agents forget what they are doing, what they agreed, and which questions are still open. On complex tasks, they blow through their context quickly. One use case for a custom memory system is to work in tandom with a transparent of the work as it happens (see this work-in-progress notebook).  Contact us to discuss your requirements for a custom memory system built around the needs of your organisation.

Also I'm not sure about the slogan, since we would be building solutions that the clients control not actually "remembering it for them".  I think the whole index.html needs some work if we're going to put it in front of potentially paying customers.

reply_text:
㊢ (progress) I've read the notebook source and the live code behind it, and found where surrounding context does and does not enter. Now reading the site's staging branch and `index.html`.㊢ (progress) The notebook edits are drafted in the source; I'm correcting one of them against the fixture turns and then building the page to a temporary file to check it evaluates.㊥ (the notebook and the site) I extended the notebook source in four places and it builds cleanly, but nothing is committed or republished. Your guess about context is half right: the system does read surrounding turns, but two kinds of context are written on every turn and never read. `@how` is also much thinner in the library than `@why`. Below are those findings, what I would change before the page goes public, and a draft for the `index.html` section.

㊢ (what I changed in `futon3c/notebooks/daxiang_live.clj`)

- **Opening:** a new paragraph saying no turn is read alone, and listing what is joined to a reply and where.
- **§2:** a sentence saying the server calls only `asks-operator?` from this file; `read-agent-turn` is used only on the page.
- **§7:** `@why` and `@how` explained as two directions that are not inverses, with `@how` as the one closer to Alexander's smaller patterns. A new cell counts both from the library files.
- **§9:** "Next" is now five numbered steps, each with the check that says whether it worked.

㊬ (what I checked) The page built to a temporary file in its own process with no evaluation errors, and the tangle test passes (2 tests, 6 assertions).

㊢ (what the code says about context) 大象 itself reads one reply and that turn's commits. The surrounding context is joined afterwards:

- **Read today:** up to 50 earlier turns of the session, the operator's turn as 象 read it, and two links between turns (an approval accepts the offer just made; a commit carries it out).
- **Resolved but unused:** your `<mark>:` pointers are matched to the agent paragraph they answer, but the port calculation never reads the result. An inline pointer such as "…and 🈸:yes" in turn 392 is not matched at all.
- **Written but not read:** the bracketed target agents put after each mark, and the pattern retrieved for each turn.

㊟ (`@how` in the library today) The new cell reports 540 `@why` links from 478 patterns, against 32 `@how` links from 21 patterns. Another 145 patterns have an `@how` line holding a sentence of instruction, not a link. So the notebook now says the cascade uses `@why` only, and that `@how` would add the downward reading: what to do when a pattern is unmet.

㊭ (before the notebook goes public)

1. **Links.** The renderer has no link markup, so the published page has no links at all: the references are plain text and nothing points back to the site.
2. **A plain opening.** A reader arriving from `index.html` needs three sentences on what the page shows and its status before meeting 小象, 象 and 大象.
3. **Internal names.** WR-26, R20, P11, "card" and a `/home/joe/...` path appear unexplained.
4. **§6.** The page itself says its premise is illustrative and its query is not a true counterfactual. I would hold it back until next-step 1 gives it a real open port.
5. **Republish.** The live copy dates from 04:45 today and predates the last three commits.
6. **Your own words.** The page shows excerpts of four of your turns. I saw nothing sensitive in the excerpts, but I did not read the full fixture files.

㊭ (the `index.html` section) I would drop the slogan. Besides your point about control, the Philip K. Dick story it quotes is about implanted false memories, which is the wrong association for a truthful record. My suggested heading is "We build memory systems that you own." A draft of your paragraph:

> We build custom memory systems for AI-assisted work on software and mathematics, where a task depends on many linked facts and decisions. Standard coding agents forget what they are doing, what they agreed, and which questions are still open, and on complex tasks they run through their context quickly. A memory system gives the agents, and you, something to consult. One use is a transparent record of the work as it happens: what was asked, offered, promised and delivered. We run a research prototype of this on our own conversations (work-in-progress notebook); it is not a product. A system built for you runs on your infrastructure and stays under your control. Contact us to discuss what your organisation needs.

I replaced "complex graphical inference" because a customer may read "graphical" as graphics; say if you want it back.

㊩ (the rest of `index.html`, for paying customers)

- **No contact route:** the only email address is on `about.html`.
- **Voice:** the page opens as "I" and switches to "we"; the margin caption is "Me running agents like a boss."
- **Unsupported claim:** the harness paragraph cites a 2019 vision and says LLMs provide it, with no link.
- **No offer:** nothing says what a first engagement looks like or who does it.

🈸 (two decisions) Shall I commit the notebook edits and pass next-steps 1 and 2 plus the link markup to claude-17, whose lane this is? And do you want the heading and paragraph applied to futon7a's `staging` branch as drafted?
